title: Tracking progress and writing a group programme that scales
audience: Trainers who run group programmes and record member progress
learningOutcomes: Choose two or three objective measures that match a member's goal and record them the same way each time
Write a group template with progressions and regressions for each movement
Explain where a group programme sits between a fully individual plan and a fixed template

instruction.heading: Track a few measures that match the goal
instruction.body: Choose two or three measures linked to the goal, such as body weight, circumference measurements, or a repeatable performance test. Use the same method each time, at a consistent time of day and on a fixed schedule. Explain to the member what each measure shows and what it cannot show. Body-composition estimates vary between methods, so compare results only within one method. Record only what the member has agreed to have recorded, and store it securely.

instruction.heading: Write one template with levels
instruction.body: A group programme can be written as one template in which each movement has a regression, a base version and a progression. Each member chooses a level at the start of a block. This sits between two extremes: a fully individual plan for each member, which takes considerable time, and a fixed daily workout that cannot change. A middle design gives much of the individual benefit at a workload a trainer can sustain.

instruction.heading: Keep a simple workout record
instruction.body: Record what each member did, the level used, any change made, and the progress measure. Review the record every four weeks and adjust the group template where several members show the same pattern.

procedure: Write the member's goal and choose two or three matching measures.
Set the schedule, time of day and method for each measure.
Write the group template with a regression, base and progression for each movement.
Log each session: level, change and measure.
Review the log every four weeks and adjust.

workedExamples.situation: A hypothetical group block includes a squat, and three members use three different levels.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How should the template show the three levels?
workedExamples.reasoning: Write the regression as a supported squat, the base as a bodyweight squat, and the progression as a loaded squat. Each member chooses a level at the start of the block. The log then shows which level each member used and when they moved up.

equipmentAndPpe: Measuring tape and scales, checked for accuracy

commonErrors.prevention: Choose two or three measures that match the goal.

commonErrors.error: Changing the measurement method partway through
commonErrors.prevention: Keep one method and note any change.

commonErrors.error: A template with one level for everyone
commonErrors.prevention: Give each movement a regression, a base and a progression.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Body-composition estimates vary by method and are not diagnostic. Do not present them as health outcomes.

qualityStandard: Each member has a goal and matching measures on record
Every movement in the template has three levels
The log is reviewed every four weeks
documentationEvidence: Member measures with method and date
summary: Track two or three measures that match the goal, using one method.
Write one template with levels for each movement.
Log and review every four weeks.

knowledgeChecks.question: A good progress tracker for a goal:
options: Records many unrelated measures every day and shares them with the members
Records two or three measures matching the goal, by the same method
Relies only on the trainer's opinion and how the member looks

knowledgeChecks.question: In a group template, a progression means:
options: An easier version of a movement
A harder version of a movement

knowledgeChecks.question: The template-to-individual scale in this lesson suggests:
options: Every member gets a unique plan from scratch in every session they attend
A middle design between individual plans and a fixed, unchanging template
No programme is needed for a group of this size at all today
